title: Checkout unavailable after release
symptoms: customers could not place orders
checkout API returned HTTP 502 responses
logs showed database acquire timeouts
problem began immediately after the release
context: The release bundled a configuration file change for the checkout service. Traffic was normal for a weekday.

suspected_causes.ruled_out_because: query durations were unchanged; requests were waiting for a connection, not for the query

confirmed_root_cause: The database connection pool size was reduced from 30 to 5 by the configuration change, so checkout requests queued waiting for a free connection.

attempted_actions.observation: database acquire timeouts returned within minutes

successful_action: Restore the connection pool size to 30 and restart the checkout service.
outcome: Orders succeeded again and the checkout error rate returned to baseline within ten minutes.
lesson_learned: When checkout failures and database timeouts begin immediately after a release, compare database connection settings with the previous working configuration before rolling back code.
verification: Connection pool saturation dropped below 60% and HTTP 502 responses stopped.

title: Checkout failing because tax service certificate expired
symptoms: checkout returned errors when orders were submitted
logs showed 'certificate has expired' when calling the tax calculation service
failures started the same morning as a checkout release
context: A checkout release went out at 09:00. The internal tax calculation service certificate was due to auto-renew that night.

suspected_causes.ruled_out_because: rolling the release back did not change the error rate

confirmed_root_cause: The TLS certificate of the internal tax calculation service expired because automatic renewal failed after its DNS validation record was deleted during a DNS cleanup.

attempted_actions.observation: orders kept failing with the same certificate error

successful_action: Restore the DNS validation record, renew the tax service certificate, and reload the service.
outcome: Tax calculation calls succeeded and checkout recovered.
lesson_learned: Same-day timing with a release is not proof the release caused it. When checkout calls to an internal dependency fail with TLS errors, check that dependency's certificate expiry and renewal status.
verification: TLS handshake to the tax service succeeded and the certificate expiry date moved 90 days out.

title: Checkout failures during payment provider outage
symptoms: customers could not complete purchases at the payment step
calls to the primary payment provider timed out
the provider's status page showed degraded service
context: A minor checkout release had shipped two hours earlier, so the team first suspected it.

suspected_causes.ruled_out_because: errors were only on outbound calls to the payment provider

confirmed_root_cause: The primary payment provider had a regional outage and its API stopped responding.

attempted_actions.observation: provider timeouts continued

successful_action: Switch card traffic to the secondary payment provider using the failover flag and queue failed payment attempts for retry.
outcome: Purchases completed through the secondary provider; queued payments were retried after the outage.
lesson_learned: When checkout fails only at the payment step and provider calls time out, check the provider status and fail over instead of restarting internal services.
verification: Payment success rate returned above 97% on the secondary provider.

title: Promo codes rejected at order placement
symptoms: orders with promotion codes failed at the final step
place-order returned HTTP 400 'invalid promotion'
orders without a code worked
context: Marketing launched a campaign with codes containing lowercase letters.
confirmed_root_cause: New promotion validation only accepted uppercase letters, so valid campaign codes were rejected.

attempted_actions.action: purge the CDN cache for the checkout page
attempted_actions.observation: API still returned 400 for the codes

successful_action: Hotfix the validation to be case-insensitive and redeploy the promotions service.
outcome: Campaign codes were accepted and affected customers were emailed a working link.
lesson_learned: When only orders with a specific input fail, look at validation rules for that input before looking at infrastructure.
verification: Promo-code orders succeeded in production smoke tests.

title: Mobile app place-order spinner never finishes
symptoms: the place-order button spun forever in the mobile app
API gateway logged HTTP 431 request header too large
the website was unaffected
context: A new mobile app version added tracking cookies to every request.
confirmed_root_cause: The mobile app sent request headers larger than the API gateway limit, so the gateway rejected the order request.

attempted_actions.observation: requests never reached the pods

successful_action: Raise the gateway header size limit temporarily and ship a mobile update that trims cookies.
outcome: Mobile orders recovered immediately after the gateway change.
lesson_learned: If only one client type fails and requests never reach the service, inspect gateway rejections such as header size limits.
verification: HTTP 431 count dropped to zero and mobile order volume returned to normal.

title: In-stock items shown as out of stock during flash sale
symptoms: customers were told items were out of stock at checkout
inventory showed plenty of stock
database reported deadlocks in reservation tables
context: Flash sale traffic combined with a new version of the inventory reservation service.
confirmed_root_cause: The new reservation service changed the order in which it locked rows, causing deadlocks that were reported to customers as out of stock.

attempted_actions.observation: deadlocks continued at the same rate

successful_action: Roll back the reservation service to the previous version.
outcome: Reservations succeeded and the sale continued.
lesson_learned: Deadlocks after a release usually mean lock ordering changed; more database capacity will not fix them.
verification: Deadlock count returned to zero and reservation success rate recovered.

title: Duplicate orders created on double click
symptoms: some customers received two identical orders
both orders were created within a second
only the new web checkout was affected
context: The web checkout had been rewritten in a new frontend framework.
confirmed_root_cause: The rewritten web checkout stopped sending the idempotency key header, so repeated submissions created separate orders.

attempted_actions.action: disable the button after the first click
attempted_actions.observation: fewer duplicates, but retries on slow networks still created them

successful_action: Restore the idempotency key header in the web checkout and cancel the duplicate orders.
outcome: No further duplicate orders; affected customers were refunded.
lesson_learned: Duplicate orders point to missing idempotency protection, not to user behaviour.
verification: Duplicate order query returned zero rows for 48 hours.

title: No shipping options for EU addresses
symptoms: customers with EU addresses saw an empty shipping options list
they could not complete checkout
US and UK customers were fine
context: A new carrier contract required updating the shipping rates table.
confirmed_root_cause: The updated shipping rates table was missing the EU country codes.

attempted_actions.observation: options list stayed empty for EU addresses

successful_action: Restore the EU rows in the shipping rates table and add a validation check for missing countries.
outcome: EU customers could select shipping and complete orders.
lesson_learned: When checkout breaks for one region only, check region-specific reference data first.
verification: Shipping quotes returned for all supported countries in a scripted check.

title: Customers charged twice after cache failover
symptoms: some customers were charged twice for one payment
payment jobs retried every 30 seconds
duplicate payment webhooks increased
context: The Redis cache cluster failed over to a replica during maintenance.
confirmed_root_cause: The cache that records already-processed payments (idempotency keys) was unavailable after the Redis failover, so retries were processed again.

attempted_actions.observation: duplicates continued because the cache was still unreachable

successful_action: Restore connectivity to the Redis primary, drain the retry backlog slowly, and refund duplicate charges.
outcome: Duplicate charges stopped and refunds were issued.
lesson_learned: A rise in duplicate payment confirmations together with retry storms usually means the duplicate-protection cache was lost.
verification: Idempotency-key hit rate returned to normal and no duplicate charges for 24 hours.

title: Card payments in Japanese yen declined
symptoms: payments in JPY were declined as 'amount too large'
other currencies worked
started after a payments release
context: The release changed how amounts are converted to minor currency units.
confirmed_root_cause: The new conversion multiplied every currency by 100, but the yen has no minor unit, so amounts sent to the provider were 100 times too large.

attempted_actions.action: open a ticket with the payment provider
attempted_actions.observation: provider confirmed requests were valid but amounts were huge

successful_action: Roll back the conversion change and add per-currency minor-unit handling.
outcome: Yen payments succeeded again.
lesson_learned: Currency-specific payment failures after a release usually come from amount or unit conversion.
verification: Test payments in JPY, EUR and USD all succeeded.

title: Refunds stuck in pending after credential rotation
symptoms: refunds stayed in 'pending' for hours
the refund worker logged 401 unauthorized from the provider
new payments were unaffected
context: Payment provider API keys were rotated the day before.
confirmed_root_cause: The refund worker still used the revoked API key because only the payment service had been updated with the new secret.

attempted_actions.observation: they failed again with 401

successful_action: Update the refund worker's secret with the new key, restart it, and requeue refunds.
outcome: All pending refunds completed.
lesson_learned: After rotating a credential, list every consumer of it; 401 errors from one worker mean it was missed.
verification: Pending refund count dropped to zero.

title: Card verification window blank
symptoms: the bank verification (3-D Secure) window was blank
customers abandoned card payments
browser console showed content security policy violations
context: Security hardening tightened the content security policy on checkout pages.
confirmed_root_cause: The new content security policy blocked the card issuer's verification frame domain.

attempted_actions.observation: the policy header was still blocking the frame

successful_action: Allow the issuer verification domains in the frame-src policy and redeploy.
outcome: Card verification displayed and payment conversion recovered.
lesson_learned: Blank embedded payment windows after security header changes point to content security policy blocks.
verification: 3-D Secure test cards completed verification.

title: Payment webhooks rejected with signature mismatch
symptoms: every webhook from the payment provider was rejected as having an invalid signature
orders stayed unpaid although customers were charged
started after a web framework upgrade
context: The payments API upgraded its web framework and body-parsing middleware.

suspected_causes.cause: the provider rotated its signing secret
suspected_causes.ruled_out_because: the secret was unchanged in the provider dashboard

confirmed_root_cause: The upgraded body parser re-serialized the JSON before signature verification, so the computed signature no longer matched the raw payload.

attempted_actions.observation: signatures still failed

successful_action: Verify the signature against the raw request body and replay the failed webhooks from the provider dashboard.
outcome: Webhooks were accepted and unpaid orders were reconciled.
lesson_learned: Signature failures after a framework upgrade usually mean the body is being modified before verification.
verification: Webhook acceptance rate returned to 100%.

title: Sign-in failures after signing certificate rotation
symptoms: sign-in took more than 8 seconds
about a quarter of sign-in attempts failed
token validation errors rose after the certificate rotation
context: The token signing certificate was rotated during planned maintenance.
confirmed_root_cause: One replica of the login service still used the previous signing certificate, so tokens it issued failed validation elsewhere.

attempted_actions.observation: failures continued at the same rate

successful_action: Update the certificate reference on the stale replica, restart it, and verify signing on every replica.
outcome: Sign-in succeeded consistently and latency returned to normal.
lesson_learned: After rotating a signing certificate, confirm every replica uses the new one; a mix causes intermittent sign-in failures.
verification: Token validation error rate returned to zero across all replicas.

title: Users logged out every few minutes
symptoms: users were signed out randomly and had to log in again
session lookups returned 'not found'
the shared Redis instance was at its memory limit
context: Sessions and the product cache shared one Redis instance; cache traffic had grown after a new feature.
confirmed_root_cause: Redis was configured to evict any key when full, so growing cache data pushed out active sessions.

attempted_actions.observation: sessions still disappeared server-side

successful_action: Move sessions to a dedicated Redis instance with no-eviction policy and more memory.
outcome: Unexpected logouts stopped.
lesson_learned: Random logouts with a full shared cache mean sessions are being evicted; keep sessions separate from cache data.
verification: Session eviction count dropped to zero.

title: Enterprise single sign-on rejected as not yet valid
symptoms: enterprise customers could not sign in with single sign-on
errors said the SAML assertion was not yet valid
started after auth servers were rebuilt from a new image
context: The authentication servers were rebuilt from a new base operating system image.
confirmed_root_cause: Time synchronisation was disabled in the new image, so the auth servers' clocks drifted several minutes behind.

attempted_actions.observation: assertions were still rejected

successful_action: Enable time synchronisation (NTP) in the image, resync clocks, and rebuild the servers.
outcome: Single sign-on worked for all enterprise customers.
lesson_learned: 'Not yet valid' or 'expired' token errors right after a server rebuild usually mean clock drift.
verification: Clock offset below 100 ms on all auth servers and SSO test logins passed.

title: Corporate customers locked out by login rate limiter
symptoms: many users from the same companies saw 'too many attempts'
individual home users could log in
started Monday morning
context: A stricter login rate limit had been introduced the previous Friday.
confirmed_root_cause: The rate limiter counted attempts per IP address, and corporate users share one office IP address.

attempted_actions.observation: lockouts decreased but brute-force protection was weakened

successful_action: Key the rate limit on account plus IP address and restore the original limit.
outcome: Corporate users could sign in and protection stayed in place.
lesson_learned: Lockouts clustered by company point to IP-based limits colliding with shared office networks.
verification: Rate-limit rejections returned to the pre-change baseline.

title: Sign-in button does nothing after frontend release
symptoms: the login page loaded but pressing sign-in did nothing
browser network tab showed requests going to the staging API
started right after a frontend release
context: The frontend build pipeline was migrated to a new CI system.
confirmed_root_cause: The production frontend was built with the staging API base URL because the new CI job did not set the production environment variable.

attempted_actions.action: ask users to clear their browser cache
attempted_actions.observation: the deployed bundle itself contained the wrong URL

successful_action: Rebuild the frontend with the production API URL and add a build check for the environment.
outcome: Sign-in worked again.
lesson_learned: If a frontend calls the wrong environment after a pipeline change, check build-time environment variables.
verification: Deployed bundle referenced the production API and login tests passed.

title: Nightly order API timeouts from reporting job
symptoms: the orders API timed out every night around 02:00
long-running transactions held locks on the orders table
daytime traffic was fine
context: A new analytics reporting job had been scheduled nightly.
confirmed_root_cause: The reporting job ran a long transaction on the primary database and held locks needed by order writes.

attempted_actions.observation: requests waited longer and connection usage grew

successful_action: Point the reporting job at the read replica and remove its write transaction.
outcome: Nightly timeouts stopped.
lesson_learned: Time-of-day timeouts usually line up with scheduled jobs; heavy reporting belongs on a replica.
verification: No lock waits on the orders table during the next three nightly runs.

title: Customers saw stale order status because of replication lag
symptoms: order status pages showed out-of-date information
database replicas were 15 minutes behind the primary
support tickets about 'order not found'
context: A data retention cleanup job had started that afternoon.
confirmed_root_cause: The cleanup job deleted millions of rows in one statement, and replicas could not replay it quickly.

attempted_actions.observation: lag grew again while replaying the same delete

successful_action: Pause the cleanup job and rewrite it to delete in small batches.
outcome: Replicas caught up within 20 minutes.
lesson_learned: Replication lag after a bulk job means the job must be batched; restarting replicas does not help.
verification: Replica lag stayed below 2 seconds during the next cleanup run.

title: Database refused connections after autoscaling
symptoms: services logged 'too many connections' from the database
errors began when the platform added application instances during a traffic spike
the database itself had spare CPU
context: Autoscaling grew the catalog service from 10 to 40 instances, each opening 20 connections.
confirmed_root_cause: Total connections from all instances (40 x 20 = 800) exceeded the database limit of 500.

attempted_actions.observation: database memory pressure increased and it had to be reverted

successful_action: Put a connection pooler in front of the database and cap instances per pool.
outcome: Connection errors stopped even at peak scale.
lesson_learned: Scaling out an application multiplies database connections; check instances times pool size against the database limit.
verification: Peak connection count stayed below 70% of the limit.

title: Query latency jumped after bulk import
symptoms: product queries became 20 times slower
the database was doing full table scans
started after a large catalog import
context: Two million products were imported overnight.
confirmed_root_cause: Table statistics were stale after the import, so the query planner chose sequential scans instead of indexes.

attempted_actions.observation: scans were still slow

successful_action: Run ANALYZE on the imported tables and schedule it after future imports.
outcome: Query times returned to normal immediately.
lesson_learned: Sudden slow queries after a large import usually mean stale planner statistics.
verification: Query plans used indexes again and p95 query time dropped below 50 ms.

title: Product search slow after cache key change
symptoms: product search took about 4 seconds
cache hit rate dropped to zero
started after the afternoon deploy
context: The deploy changed the format of search cache keys.
confirmed_root_cause: The new cache key format never matched existing entries, so every search went to the database.

attempted_actions.observation: slightly faster but the database stayed overloaded

successful_action: Fix the cache key format and pre-warm the most common searches.
outcome: Search latency returned to about 200 ms.
lesson_learned: If latency jumps after a deploy and cache hit rate collapses, check cache key changes.
verification: Cache hit rate back above 85%.

title: Web API slow from memory pressure pauses
symptoms: API response times doubled in the afternoon
restarting the service helped for about an hour
long garbage-collection pauses in the logs
context: Container memory limits had been reduced to save cost.
confirmed_root_cause: The lower container memory limit left the Java heap too small, causing frequent long garbage-collection pauses.

attempted_actions.observation: latency improved briefly then degraded again

successful_action: Restore the container memory limit and set the heap size explicitly.
outcome: Response times stabilised.
lesson_learned: A slow service that recovers briefly after each restart points to memory pressure, not a code bug.
verification: GC pause time below 50 ms per minute.

title: Order history page slow from N+1 queries
symptoms: the order history page took over 6 seconds for long-time customers
hundreds of small database queries per page view
started after an ORM refactor
context: The data access layer was refactored to a new ORM pattern.
confirmed_root_cause: The refactor loaded each order's items with a separate query (N+1 queries).

attempted_actions.observation: the number of queries per page was unchanged

successful_action: Load order items together with orders in one query (eager loading).
outcome: Page load dropped to under 500 ms.
lesson_learned: Pages that get slower for customers with more data usually have per-item queries.
verification: Queries per page view dropped from hundreds to three.

title: Latency spikes every hour on the hour
symptoms: API latency spiked for five minutes at the start of every hour
CPU on some nodes hit 100% at those times
no deploys correlated
context: A log compression cron job had been added to the shared nodes.
confirmed_root_cause: The hourly log compression job ran on the same nodes as the API and consumed all CPU.
successful_action: Move the compression job to dedicated nodes and set CPU limits.
outcome: Hourly spikes disappeared.
lesson_learned: Regular, clock-aligned latency spikes usually come from scheduled jobs on shared hosts.
verification: p99 latency flat across hour boundaries for a week.

title: Website slow only for visitors in Asia
symptoms: pages and images loaded slowly for visitors in Asia
Europe and US were fast
started after moving DNS to a new provider
context: DNS records were migrated to a new provider the day before.
confirmed_root_cause: Geo-routing records were not migrated, so Asian visitors were sent to the US origin instead of the nearby CDN edge.

attempted_actions.observation: requests still bypassed the Asian edge

successful_action: Recreate the geo-routing records at the new DNS provider.
outcome: Asian visitors were served from nearby edges again.
lesson_learned: Region-specific slowness after a DNS migration points to missing geo-routing records.
verification: Median page load in Asia back under 2 seconds.

title: Homepage errors after feature flag default flipped
symptoms: the homepage showed an error for many visitors
an unfinished recommendations widget appeared for others
started after a feature flag service upgrade
context: The feature flag service was upgraded to a new configuration schema.
confirmed_root_cause: In the new schema, flags without an explicit value defaulted to on, enabling an unfinished feature.

attempted_actions.observation: the flag was controlled outside the website

successful_action: Explicitly set the recommendations flag to off and audit all flags for implicit defaults.
outcome: Homepage recovered.
lesson_learned: When unfinished features suddenly appear, check feature flag defaults before rolling back code.
verification: Flag audit showed every flag with an explicit value.

title: Pods crash-looping after full rollout
symptoms: the canary looked healthy
after full rollout, pods restarted repeatedly (CrashLoopBackOff)
logs said a required setting was missing
context: The release required a new environment variable.
confirmed_root_cause: The new variable existed in the canary namespace but not in the main production secret set.

attempted_actions.observation: they crashed with the same missing-setting error

successful_action: Add the missing variable to the production secret set and redeploy.
outcome: Pods started normally.
lesson_learned: A canary that passes but full rollout that crashes points to configuration that differs between environments.
verification: All pods ready and configuration diff between canary and production empty.

title: Internal services unreachable after infrastructure apply
symptoms: internal services timed out calling each other
external traffic reached the load balancer but requests failed
started right after an infrastructure-as-code apply
context: An engineer ran an infrastructure apply to fix configuration drift.
confirmed_root_cause: The apply removed a manually added firewall rule that allowed service-to-service traffic.

attempted_actions.observation: network connections were still blocked

successful_action: Restore the firewall rule and add it to the infrastructure code.
outcome: Service-to-service traffic resumed.
lesson_learned: Network timeouts right after an infrastructure apply usually mean a rule was removed; compare the plan output.
verification: Connectivity checks between all services passed.

title: EU requests routed to US endpoint
symptoms: EU customers got errors when viewing their account data
requests were sent to the US data endpoint
started after a configuration template change
context: Region configuration moved to a shared template.
confirmed_root_cause: The shared template fell back to the default US region when the EU region value was missing.
successful_action: Set the EU region explicitly in the template and make a missing region fail the deploy.
outcome: EU requests went to the EU endpoint again.
lesson_learned: Silent defaults in shared configuration templates can send traffic to the wrong place; make required values fail loudly.
verification: Region routing test passed for every region.

title: Emails contained links to the staging site
symptoms: password reset and order emails linked to the staging website
customers reported broken links
started after a notifications release
context: The notifications service moved to environment-based settings.
confirmed_root_cause: The production BASE_URL setting was copied from staging.
successful_action: Correct the BASE_URL setting and resend affected emails.
outcome: New emails contained correct links.
lesson_learned: Wrong-environment links point to environment settings copied between stages.
verification: Test emails linked to the production domain.

title: API servers out of disk from debug logging
symptoms: the API returned HTTP 500 errors
logs said 'no space left on device'
the log directory was using almost all disk space
context: Debug logging had been enabled during an investigation the previous week.
confirmed_root_cause: Debug logging was never turned off and filled the disks.

attempted_actions.observation: freed temporary files but disks filled again within an hour

successful_action: Turn off debug logging, rotate and delete old logs, and add a disk usage alert.
outcome: Errors stopped and disk usage stayed below 40%.
lesson_learned: 'No space left on device' with a large log directory means logging is too verbose or not rotated.
verification: Disk usage stable for 48 hours.

title: Database writes failed with full volume
symptoms: database writes failed
the database volume was 100% full
write-ahead log files were piling up
context: A replica had been decommissioned the week before.
confirmed_root_cause: A replication slot for the decommissioned replica kept all write-ahead logs from being cleaned up.

attempted_actions.action: delete old application logs from the volume
attempted_actions.observation: freed very little space

successful_action: Drop the stale replication slot and expand the volume.
outcome: Writes resumed and space was reclaimed.
lesson_learned: Growing write-ahead logs usually mean an abandoned replication slot.
verification: WAL directory size returned to normal and slot list contained only active replicas.

title: Image uploads failing because storage quota reached
symptoms: customers could not upload profile and product images
object storage returned quota exceeded
temporary upload folder was huge
context: Storage lifecycle rules were cleaned up the month before.
confirmed_root_cause: The rule that deleted temporary uploads after a day had been removed, so the bucket reached its quota.
successful_action: Restore the lifecycle rule and purge old temporary uploads.
outcome: Uploads worked again.
lesson_learned: Quota errors on object storage often come from missing cleanup rules.
verification: Bucket usage dropped by 70%.

title: Pods evicted because node disks filled with images
symptoms: pods were evicted from several nodes
nodes reported disk pressure
many old container images were on the nodes
context: Deploys had become more frequent with larger images.
confirmed_root_cause: Container image garbage collection thresholds were too high, so old images filled node disks.

attempted_actions.observation: new nodes filled up after a few days

successful_action: Lower image garbage-collection thresholds and prune unused images.
outcome: Evictions stopped.
lesson_learned: Disk pressure evictions on busy clusters usually come from image accumulation.
verification: Node disk usage below 60% for a week.

title: Backups silently failing
symptoms: a restore test found the latest backup was 12 days old
backup jobs had been failing
no one received alerts
context: Alert routing had been reorganised between teams.
confirmed_root_cause: The backup target disk was full and the failure alert was routed to a retired channel.
successful_action: Expand the backup disk, run a full backup, and route alerts to the on-call rotation.
outcome: Backups resumed and a restore test succeeded.
lesson_learned: Test restores regularly and verify alert routing when teams reorganise.
verification: Successful restore from the new backup.

title: Mobile apps could not connect after certificate authority change
symptoms: iOS and Android apps showed connection errors
browsers worked normally
started after renewing the API certificate with a new certificate authority
context: Older app versions pin the previous certificate authority.
confirmed_root_cause: Certificate pinning in the apps rejected the certificate from the new certificate authority.

attempted_actions.observation: apps still rejected the certificate

successful_action: Reissue the certificate from the previous certificate authority and plan a pin update in the next app release.
outcome: Apps connected again.
lesson_learned: If apps fail but browsers work after a certificate change, check certificate pinning.
verification: Older app versions connected in device tests.

title: Partner API calls failed with incomplete certificate chain
symptoms: a partner reported 'unable to verify the first certificate'
our own browser tests passed
started after moving to a new load balancer
context: The partner API moved to a new load balancer.
confirmed_root_cause: Only the leaf certificate was installed on the new load balancer; the intermediate certificate was missing.
successful_action: Upload the full certificate chain to the load balancer.
outcome: Partner calls succeeded.
lesson_learned: Browsers can hide missing intermediate certificates; test with strict clients after load balancer changes.
verification: SSL checker reported a complete chain.

title: Service-to-service mTLS failures after CA rotation
symptoms: some internal calls failed with 'unknown certificate authority'
only certain service pairs were affected
started after the internal certificate authority was rotated
context: The internal mutual TLS certificate authority was rotated.
confirmed_root_cause: Several services still had the old trust bundle and did not trust certificates signed by the new authority.

attempted_actions.observation: it loaded the same stale trust bundle

successful_action: Distribute a trust bundle containing both old and new authorities and roll it out everywhere.
outcome: All internal calls succeeded.
lesson_learned: Rotate certificate authorities with an overlap period where both are trusted.
verification: mTLS handshake errors dropped to zero.

title: Custom domains showed 'not secure' warnings
symptoms: customer sites on custom domains showed browser security warnings
certificates had expired
renewal logs showed rate limit errors from the certificate authority
context: A bug in the renewal job reissued certificates repeatedly.
confirmed_root_cause: The renewal loop hit the certificate authority's rate limit, so real renewals were refused.

attempted_actions.action: re-run renewal for all domains at once
attempted_actions.observation: hit the rate limit again

successful_action: Fix the renewal loop and renew domains in staggered batches.
outcome: All custom domains had valid certificates again.
lesson_learned: Mass certificate renewals must be staggered to stay under authority rate limits.
verification: Certificate expiry monitor green for all domains.

title: Order emails delayed by poison message
symptoms: order confirmation emails arrived hours late
email workers crashed and restarted repeatedly
all crashes happened on the same message
context: A customer name contained characters the template engine could not handle.
confirmed_root_cause: One malformed message crashed every worker that picked it up, blocking the queue because there was no dead-letter queue.

attempted_actions.observation: every new worker crashed on the same message

successful_action: Move the poison message to a new dead-letter queue and fix the template encoding.
outcome: The backlog cleared within 30 minutes.
lesson_learned: If all workers crash on the same message, isolate it with a dead-letter queue instead of scaling.
verification: Queue depth back to zero and dead-letter queue monitored.

title: Job backlog grew after worker concurrency dropped
symptoms: the fulfilment job queue kept growing after a release
workers were healthy but slow
each worker processed one job at a time
context: The release renamed several environment variables.
confirmed_root_cause: The worker concurrency variable was renamed, so workers fell back to a default of 1 instead of 50.

attempted_actions.observation: backlog grew more slowly but did not shrink

successful_action: Set the renamed concurrency variable back to 50 and redeploy.
outcome: The backlog drained within an hour.
lesson_learned: When throughput drops after a release but workers are healthy, check concurrency settings for silent defaults.
verification: Jobs processed per minute returned to the previous level.

title: Inventory updates applied twice
symptoms: stock counts went negative for popular items
the same inventory message was processed twice
processing time had increased
context: A new validation step made inventory processing slower.
confirmed_root_cause: Processing now took longer than the queue visibility timeout, so messages were redelivered while still being processed.
successful_action: Increase the visibility timeout and make the consumer idempotent.
outcome: No more duplicate inventory updates.
lesson_learned: Duplicate processing after work got slower points to visibility timeouts shorter than processing time.
verification: No duplicate message IDs processed for a week.

title: Event stream consumer lag from rebalance storm
symptoms: analytics dashboards were hours behind
consumer group rebalanced every few minutes
some partitions were not being read
context: A slower enrichment step was added to the consumer.
confirmed_root_cause: Handling a batch took longer than the maximum poll interval, so consumers were kicked out and the group kept rebalancing.

attempted_actions.observation: rebalancing resumed after the first slow batch

successful_action: Reduce the batch size and raise the maximum poll interval.
outcome: Lag caught up overnight.
lesson_learned: Constant rebalancing means consumers take too long per batch.
verification: Consumer lag below one minute.

title: Nightly invoice job did not run
symptoms: nightly invoices were not generated
the scheduler reported that another instance held the job lock
no instance was actually running the job
context: A scheduler node crashed the evening before.
confirmed_root_cause: The crashed node left its leader lock in Redis without an expiry, so no other scheduler would start the job.
successful_action: Clear the stale lock, run the job manually, and add an expiry to the lock.
outcome: Invoices were generated and sent the same morning.
lesson_learned: Distributed locks must expire; a crashed holder can block scheduled work indefinitely.
verification: Scheduler ran the job the following night without intervention.

title: Sign-up verification texts not delivered in one country
symptoms: new users in Brazil did not receive SMS verification codes
sign-ups there dropped sharply
the SMS vendor accepted messages but delivery reports failed
context: The SMS vendor changed carrier routes in some countries.
confirmed_root_cause: The SMS vendor's route for Brazil was throttled by the local carrier.

attempted_actions.observation: resent messages were also not delivered

successful_action: Route Brazil traffic through the backup SMS vendor.
outcome: Codes were delivered and sign-ups recovered.
lesson_learned: Country-specific delivery failures point to vendor routing; keep a fallback vendor.
verification: Delivery success rate for Brazil back above 95%.

title: Address autocomplete failures slowed checkout form
symptoms: the address field hung for several seconds
the autocomplete vendor returned quota exceeded
checkout completion rate dipped
context: A marketing campaign increased traffic 5 times.
confirmed_root_cause: The address autocomplete API key hit its daily quota.
successful_action: Raise the vendor quota and add a short timeout with manual address entry as fallback.
outcome: The form stayed responsive even when the vendor was slow.
lesson_learned: Every third-party call on the purchase path needs a timeout and a fallback.
verification: Address field responded within 300 ms in load tests.

title: Shipping labels failed after carrier API change
symptoms: shipping labels could not be created
the carrier API responses had a new format
no change had been made on our side
context: The carrier released a new API version without notice.
confirmed_root_cause: The carrier changed its default API version, and our parser did not understand the new response format.

attempted_actions.observation: same parse errors

successful_action: Pin the carrier API version in requests and update the parser.
outcome: Labels were created and the backlog shipped.
lesson_learned: Always pin third-party API versions explicitly.
verification: Label creation success rate at 100%.

title: Site unreachable for some users during DNS provider outage
symptoms: some users could not reach the website at all
DNS lookups failed intermittently
the DNS provider reported an incident
context: All DNS was hosted with a single provider.
confirmed_root_cause: The only DNS provider had a partial outage.

attempted_actions.observation: did not help while the provider was failing

successful_action: Add a secondary DNS provider with synchronised records.
outcome: Resolution recovered; later provider incidents had no customer impact.
lesson_learned: A single DNS provider is a single point of failure.
verification: Both DNS providers answered for all records.
